gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 23.4 lb Jackery HomePower 1000 v2 has a LiFePO4 battery, charges from up to 400 W of solar through two DC8020 ports, charges from a car's 12 V socket (8 A max, about 11 h), and keeps charging down to 14°F (−10°C). The Explorer 1000 v2 and Anker C1000 Gen 2 stop charging at 32°F (0°C).
standout_why: I compared our own page, backup-power.org (cited in four chats), and the seven saved ChatGPT answers. Our page lists the HomePower 1000 v2's solar input as 'none listed' and calls it 'a home-backup box, not a camping one'. Every ChatGPT answer repeats that: 'lacks a listed solar charging input', 'Not confirmed'. backup-power.org lists the 12 V sockets only as outputs, says nothing about charging temperature, and leaves out the HomePower 1000 v2. One chat (r2, citing Jackery's FAQ) gives the Explorer 1000 v2's roughly 12 h car-socket charge time. No page has the HomePower's solar and car inputs or any model's lowest charging temperature.
decides: This changes the pick. The one reason ChatGPT and our page gave for passing over the lightest unit (no solar input) is wrong, according to Jackery's own help center. The HomePower 1000 v2 weighs 10.6 kg (23.4 lb) with 1,024 Wh of LiFePO4. It takes 400 W of solar on the same DC8020 ports as the Explorer, and it charges from the car. That makes it the lightest 1,000 Wh-class LiFePO4 station that recharges off-grid. It is 0.4 lb lighter than the Explorer 1000 v2, though it holds 46 Wh less, so the Explorer still has more Wh per pound (45.0 against 43.8). It also takes a charge down to 14°F, while the Explorer 1000 v2 and the Anker C1000 Gen 2 stop at 32°F. That matters for shoulder-season car camping. Three limits apply to both Jackerys. Car-socket charging is capped at 8 A, roughly 100 W, so a full refill takes about 11–12 h of driving. Anything faster needs Jackery's car fast charger (about 2.7–3 h). The HomePower cannot take solar and car charging at the same time. The Solar Lab measured 22 W of idle draw on the HomePower, and says the car charging cable is not included.

findings.value: 16–60 V, 12 A max per port, 21 A / 400 W max across two DC8020 ports
findings.note: Jackery's wording: '16V-60V=12A Max, Double to 21A Max/ 400W Max'. This contradicts 'none listed' on our page. The Solar Lab's review also describes two 200 W inputs, 400 W total.

findings.label: Car-socket charging input and time
findings.value: 11–16 V, 8 A max on one DC8020 port; about 11 h for a full charge; 2.7 h with Jackery's car fast charger
findings.note: 8 A × 12–14 V ≈ 96–112 W. 1,024 Wh ÷ ~100 W ≈ 10–11 h, which matches Jackery's '≈11H'. Jackery says solar and car charging at the same time is 'Not supported'.

findings.note: The discharging range is the same, 14°F to 113°F.
